summary: Twenty finite SV.0 declarations on the existing BoundingSieve carrier. All eight inherited nodes remain unchanged. Twelve additions construct multiplicity-preserving finite-family and arbitrary-residue sieves, remove zero-density local conditions, separate full-residue obstructions, prove their exact divisibility/survival interfaces and transfer the Legendre error bound. Dimension, distribution and advanced endpoints remain open; no new sieve carrier or generic multiplicative extension is introduced.

nodes.title: Weighted divisibility interchange
nodes.statement: For every coefficient function c:N→R, sum_{d|P} c(d) A_d = sum_{n in A} w(n) sum_{d|gcd(P,n)} c(d).
hypotheses: s is the existing BoundingSieve: P=s.prodPrimes, A=s.support, w=s.weights, X=s.totalMass, nu=s.nu; A_d=s.multSum(d), R_d=s.rem(d), S=s.siftedSum. Divisors are positive natural divisors.
c is arbitrary; its values need not be nonnegative.
proofSteps: Expand each A_d and interchange two finite sums; retain c(d) with its sign.
For each n, divisibility by both P and n is equivalent to divisibility by gcd(P,n). Since P is nonzero and gcd(P,n) divides P, apply Nat.divisors_filter_dvd_of_dvd to identify the inner finite set.
acceptance: For P=1 this reduces to c(1) times the total support weight, including a possible weight at zero.
For P=6 the four divisor coefficients account separately for 1,2,3,6; no coprimality condition is imposed on n.

sources.match: Same finite interchange, extended to arbitrary real coefficients and the existing weighted carrier.

nodes.title: Exact Legendre sieve identity
nodes.statement: S = sum_{d|P} mu(d) A_d, where mu is the existing integer Möbius function cast to R.
hypotheses: s is the existing BoundingSieve: P=s.prodPrimes, A=s.support, w=s.weights, X=s.totalMass, nu=s.nu; A_d=s.multSum(d), R_d=s.rem(d), S=s.siftedSum. Divisors are positive natural divisors.
proofSteps: Specialize the weighted interchange to c(d)=mu(d).
The existing identity mu*zeta=1, evaluated using the existing convolution-with-zeta formula and arithmetic-function unit, gives sum_{d|r}mu(d)=1 if r=1 and zero otherwise.
Set r=gcd(P,n) and identify the existing sifted-sum indicator. This also covers n=0, since P is nonzero.
acceptance: Empty support gives zero; P=1 returns all support weight.
For support {1,...,10}, P=6 and unit weights, S=10-5-3+1=3.
For support {0,1,2,3,6}, P=6 and unit weights, S=5-3-3+2=1: zero must be excluded.

sources.match: The exact unweighted identity is specialized to the pinned weighted carrier; Kedlaya Chapter 11, Lemma 11.2 is the weighted inclusion-exclusion motivation.

nodes.title: Euler-product main term with signed remainder
nodes.statement: S = X product_{p in primeFactors(P)}(1-nu(p)) + sum_{d|P} mu(d)R_d.
hypotheses: s is the existing BoundingSieve: P=s.prodPrimes, A=s.support, w=s.weights, X=s.totalMass, nu=s.nu; A_d=s.multSum(d), R_d=s.rem(d), S=s.siftedSum. Divisors are positive natural divisors.
No sign assumption on X and no normalization X=A_1 is added.
proofSteps: Substitute A_d=nu(d)X+R_d into the exact Legendre identity, distribute the finite sum and factor out X.
Apply the existing squarefree multiplicative Euler-product identity with f=nu and n=P. Keep the remainder sum signed.
acceptance: For P=1 the identity reads A_1=X+R_1.
For P=6 the signed error is R_1-R_2-R_3+R_6.

sources.match: Use nu(d)=omega(d)/d, with multiplicativity only on coprime arguments; the pinned carrier already contains the needed data.

nodes.title: Absolute Legendre error bound
nodes.statement: |S-X product_{p in primeFactors(P)}(1-nu(p))| <= sum_{d|P}|R_d|.
hypotheses: s is the existing BoundingSieve: P=s.prodPrimes, A=s.support, w=s.weights, X=s.totalMass, nu=s.nu; A_d=s.multSum(d), R_d=s.rem(d), S=s.siftedSum. Divisors are positive natural divisors.
proofSteps: Subtract the Euler-product term in the exact identity.
Apply the triangle inequality to the finite signed sum. Every d dividing squarefree P is squarefree, so |mu(d)|=1.
Do not drop the divisor d=1 unless the additional normalization X=A_1 has actually been proved.
acceptance: With P=1, A_1=10 and X=7 the error is exactly |R_1|=3.
The right-hand side is nonnegative even when X is negative.

sources.match: Exact same remainder bound, with nonnegative real weights instead of unit weights.

nodes.title: Lower sieve coefficient inequality
nodes.statement: If c:N→R satisfies sum_{d|r} c(d) <= 1_{r=1} for every r dividing P, then sum_{d|P}c(d)A_d <= S.
hypotheses: s is the existing BoundingSieve: P=s.prodPrimes, A=s.support, w=s.weights, X=s.totalMass, nu=s.nu; A_d=s.multSum(d), R_d=s.rem(d), S=s.siftedSum. Divisors are positive natural divisors.
The displayed lower coefficient condition is required only for positive divisors r of this P, not for all naturals.
proofSteps: Apply the coefficient condition at r=gcd(P,n), which divides P.
Multiply the pointwise inequality by the nonnegative w(n), sum over the finite support and use the weighted interchange.
Use the existing coprimality-indicator presentation of S. Coefficients c may have either sign.
acceptance: c=mu on the divisors of P gives equality.
For P=1 the coefficient condition is just c(1)<=1, and the result applies to any nonnegative weight at zero.

sources.match: The source's lower coefficient condition; the proof is the same weighted interchange as for its displayed upper bound.

nodes.title: Lower main term minus absolute remainder
nodes.statement: Under the lower coefficient condition, X mainSum(c) - errSum(c) <= S, using exactly the existing mainSum and errSum.
hypotheses: s is the existing BoundingSieve: P=s.prodPrimes, A=s.support, w=s.weights, X=s.totalMass, nu=s.nu; A_d=s.multSum(d), R_d=s.rem(d), S=s.siftedSum. Divisors are positive natural divisors.
For every r dividing P, sum_{d|r}c(d)<=1_{r=1}.
proofSteps: Expand each A_d in the lower coefficient inequality and collect X sum c(d)nu(d).
For every d, c(d)R_d >= -|c(d)||R_d|. Sum this inequality and identify the existing error term.
No multiplication of an inequality by X occurs, so no nonnegativity hypothesis on X is needed.
acceptance: The zero coefficient function yields the elementary inequality 0<=S.
Choosing c=mu recovers the lower half of the absolute Legendre estimate.
Opposite coefficient signs do not permit cancellation inside errSum.

sources.locator: Section 1, p.5, (1.5) and the main/error calculation (1.7)-(1.8)
sources.match: Lower analogue of the source's upper main/error estimate, on the pinned carrier.

nodes.title: Remainder bound at a coefficient cutoff
nodes.statement: Let D be a natural number and C a nonnegative real. If c(d)=0 for every d|P with D<d, and |c(d)|<=C for d|P with d<=D, then errSum(c)<=C sum_{d|P,d<=D}|R_d|.
hypotheses: s is the existing BoundingSieve: P=s.prodPrimes, A=s.support, w=s.weights, X=s.totalMass, nu=s.nu; A_d=s.multSum(d), R_d=s.rem(d), S=s.siftedSum. Divisors are positive natural divisors.
D>=0 is an integer cutoff; the bound includes d=D.
The support and absolute-coefficient assumptions are both necessary inputs; they are stated explicitly, not packaged in a new predicate.
proofSteps: Split the divisor sum into d<=D and D<d. The latter terms vanish by the support condition.
On each remaining term multiply |c(d)|<=C by the nonnegative |R_d| and sum. Factor out C.
This is exact finite bookkeeping; a separate family estimate is required to bound the remaining sum asymptotically.
acceptance: For D=0 the supported divisor coefficients all vanish, so errSum=0.
For c(1)=1 and c(d)=0 at every other divisor, errSum=|R_1|; D=1 does not remove mass error.
If P=6, c(2)=1, c(3)=-1, other divisor coefficients zero, and R_2=R_3=1, the error equals 2, not zero.

sources.locator: Section 1, p.5, (1.8); Section 2, p.7, support condition before the quadratic-form calculation
sources.match: Extracts the explicit consequence of small coefficient support from the source error term; does not claim that SelbergSieve.level proves a remainder distribution estimate.

nodes.title: First Bonferroni lower sieve bound
nodes.statement: A_1 - sum_{p in primeFactors(P)} A_p <= S.
hypotheses: s is the existing BoundingSieve: P=s.prodPrimes, A=s.support, w=s.weights, X=s.totalMass, nu=s.nu; A_d=s.multSum(d), R_d=s.rem(d), S=s.siftedSum. Divisors are positive natural divisors.
proofSteps: For each n, let k count the sieving primes dividing n. If gcd(P,n)=1 then k=0; otherwise the existing prime-divisor existence theorem gives a prime dividing both P and n, so k>=1.
Thus 1-k<=1_{gcd(P,n)=1}. Multiply by the nonnegative weight and sum over support.
Interchange the finite prime and support sums to identify A_1 and the A_p terms.
acceptance: For P=1 there are no sieving primes, so equality holds.
For support {6}, P=6 and weight 1 at 6, the left side is -1 and S=0.
This bound can be negative; it does not imply a positive lower bound for primes or evade sieve parity.

sources.locator: Section 11.2, Lemma 11.1 and its pointwise proof; compare Heath-Brown p.5 (1.5)
sources.match: First lower truncation of the pointwise inclusion-exclusion count, proved directly for the nonnegative weights of BoundingSieve.

nodes.title: Weighted finite-family sieve
nodes.statement: Construct s.ofFiniteFamily(A,f,w) as a BoundingSieve with support f(A), weight at n equal to Σ_{a∈A,f(a)=n}w(a), and the same prime product, density and approximate mass as s.
hypotheses: s is an existing BoundingSieve; A is a finite set of indices in any type; f maps indices to naturals; w is real-valued and nonnegative on A. No injectivity or positivity of f is assumed.
proofSteps: Use the existing BoundingSieve record, replacing only support and weights by the displayed finite image and fiber sums.
Every fiber weight is nonnegative because all its indices belong to A. Retain the template's squarefreeness and both strict prime-density bounds unchanged.

The projection and off-image API follow from the record and finite sums. For identity-family compatibility, interchange finite fibers using the existing additive fiber theorem; only observables, not unrestricted off-support weights, agree.
acceptance: All repeated labels contribute to the weight; this is not an unweighted image sieve.
The map may take the value zero. Its divisibility and survival follow the existing natural conventions.
Replacing a population does not prove that the retained X approximates its mass.

nodes.title: Divisibility sums of a weighted family
nodes.statement: For every natural d, multSum(d) of s.ofFiniteFamily(A,f,w) equals Σ_{a∈A,d|f(a)}w(a).
hypotheses: s is an existing BoundingSieve; A is a finite set of indices in any type; f maps indices to naturals; w is real-valued and nonnegative on A. No injectivity or positivity of f is assumed.
proofSteps: Expand only the new support and weights and the existing multSum.
Use Finset's generated additive fiberwise identity on the finite image restricted by d dividing the image value.
An index lies over that restricted image exactly when d divides its label; no injectivity is used. In particular d=0 picks exactly zero labels.

nodes.title: Prime divisibility of a residue label
nodes.statement: Let Q be a finite set of primes and Ωp a finite subset of ZMod p. For any integer a and p∈Q, p divides L(a)=∏_{q∈Q,a mod q∈Ωq}q if and only if a mod p belongs to Ωp.
hypotheses: No properness, nonemptiness, sign or interval condition is needed for Ω or a.
proofSteps: The factors in L(a) are distinct primes, so the existing primeFactors_prod theorem identifies its prime-factor set with the defining filtered set.
The product is nonzero, including when the filter is empty.
Apply prime-factor membership at the prime p and use p∈Q to eliminate the redundant membership condition.
acceptance: The result handles negative integers by the existing integer cast to ZMod.
An empty bad set can never contribute its prime to the label.

nodes.title: Simultaneous local conditions as divisibility
nodes.statement: Under the same finite prime data, for every d dividing ∏_{p∈Q}p and every integer a, d divides L(a) if and only if a mod p belongs to Ωp for every p∈primeFactors(d).
hypotheses: The divisor hypothesis is on the squarefree prime product; d=1 is allowed, and d=0 is excluded by that hypothesis.
proofSteps: Distinct primes are pairwise coprime, so the existing squarefree-product theorem makes the ambient product squarefree; hence its divisor d is squarefree.
Replace d by the product of its prime factors. Use prod_primeFactors_dvd_iff and primeFactors_prod to translate divisibility into containment of prime supports.
Every prime of d already lies in Q because d divides the ambient product, leaving precisely the displayed simultaneous residue conditions.

Do not extend to d=4 with Q={2}: a label containing the prime 2 once is not divisible by 4.

nodes.title: Sieve with arbitrary excluded residue classes
nodes.statement: Construct BoundingSieve.ofResidueClasses(A,x,w,Q,Ω,X) with prime product P, multiplicative density prodPrimeFactors(ρ), approximate mass X, support the image of L∘x on A, and weights the sums over its fibers.
hypotheses: A is a finite index set, x maps indices to integers, w is real-valued and nonnegative on A, Q is a finite set consisting of primes, Ωp is a finite subset of ZMod p for each natural p, card(Ωp)

Write ρ(p)=card(Ωp)/p, Q+= {p∈Q : Ωp is nonempty}, P=∏_{p∈Q+}p and L(b)=∏_{p∈Q,b mod p∈Ωp}p. All products are finite, with empty product 1. These are local expressions, not new carriers or functions in the blueprint.
proofSteps: Remove precisely the empty local sets to form Q+. The product P is squarefree by the existing distinct-prime product theorem.
Use the existing arithmetic function prodPrimeFactors(ρ), not a new multiplicative-extension construction. Its prime value is ρ(p), and its value at zero is zero.
For p∈Q+, nonempty Ωp gives ρ(p)>0; the properness hypothesis gives ρ(p)<1. Empty densities occur only outside P, where the carrier imposes no strict bound.
Build the existing carrier with this prime/density/mass data and apply finite-family-sieve to the label map L∘x. This supplies global nonnegativity of the fiber weights.
Verify the projection, prime-value and inactive-prime API directly. The supported divisibility and sifted-sum laws are separate promoted lemma nodes because the error theorem consumes them.
acceptance: All-empty local data are valid and give P=1. Do not impose card(Ωp)>0 on the original Q.
If a local set has card p, use full-residue-obstruction rather than forcing density 1 into this carrier.
The chosen density extension is only multiplicative on coprime inputs: at prime powers it repeats no factor. On the squarefree divisors actually used, it is exactly the product of local densities.
The natural labels record local membership, not the magnitude of the original integer samples; no linear cutoff follows.
